evals.prompt: Make me a one-page photo consent form as a fillable PDF - full name, email, date and a signature.
evals.expected_output: A one-page fillable PDF. Full name, email and date are real form widgets. The signature area is labelled but carries no widget and no printed line - it is left as empty space.
assertions: The output is a single-page PDF file
Full name, email and date are interactive form fields, not printed labels alone
The signature area contains no form widget of any kind
The signature area contains no drawn line, underscore run, or box border
The consent text names what is being consented to rather than using placeholder text

evals.prompt: Patient intake form. I need the ID document scanned but we must not keep the picture - only the name and document number.
evals.expected_output: A fillable PDF whose identity section uses the machine-readable-zone attributes so no image is stored, with the named fields receiving the scanned values as text.
assertions: The identity trigger is combined with machine-readable-zone attributes rather than used alone
No field is configured to receive the front-side image of the document
Each field that receives a verified value is paired in the same field name as the trigger
The reply states explicitly that no image of the document will be stored

evals.prompt: Same tenancy form but there are two tenants and both need to be identity-checked.
evals.expected_output: One document with two independent identity groups, indexed per person, and one signature area each.
assertions: Identity attributes are indexed per person, so the two tenants do not share a group
Each tenant has exactly one identity trigger, not two in the same group
There is one signature area per tenant
No signature area is a form widget

evals.prompt: Build me a fillable rental application PDF. Use whatever Python libraries you need.
evals.expected_output: A fillable PDF built with a library that is already present, or with the standard library alone. No installer runs: "use whatever you need" is not consent to install anything.
assertions: No package installer is run — no pip, uv, npm, brew, winget, or virtual environment — because the user never said yes to a named list of packages
pymupdf and fitz are not used
No headless browser or HTML-to-PDF converter is used
If no library from the closed list is present, the reply falls back to the standard-library recipe before considering anything else
The reply names which rung produced the file

evals.prompt: I'm in Codex on my Windows laptop, nothing extra installed. Make me a fillable deposit receipt PDF: seller, buyer, amount, date, and a signature for each of them.
evals.expected_output: There is no PDF library and no Python on a stock Windows PC, so the reply is the hand-over in its fixed shape: the complete receipt text with field names in double braces, a field table with one row per field, the two signature areas, and the one step that remains. Nothing is installed and no install is proposed.
assertions: The reply contains the complete document text, not a summary, with each field marked in double braces where it belongs
There is a field table with one row per field carrying name, label, kind, required, page and anchor
Both signature areas are listed as empty space with a caption, and neither is a form widget
The reply names the single remaining step and where it can be done
No installation of Python, a library, or a browser is run or proposed
The reply does not apologise or say that a PDF cannot be made; it says which rung produced this result

evals.prompt: Napravi mi PDF obrazac suglasnosti s poljima ime i prezime, OIB, datum i potpis. Ovdje imam samo Python, bez dodatnih paketa.
evals.expected_output: The standard-library rung applies, but the Croatian text needs č, ć and đ, which Helvetica in WinAnsi cannot carry. The reply says so before building anything, and offers the two ways forward: an isolated install of named packages after an explicit yes, or the hand-over. It does not install before the user answers.
assertions: The reply states that the standard-library route cannot render č, ć or đ and does not ship a file with replaced characters
The reply offers an isolated install by naming the exact packages and the folder, and asks a yes/no question
Nothing is installed before the user answers that question
The hand-over is offered as the alternative in the same message
The signature area is described as empty space with a caption, never as a form field
OIB is a text field, not something the user is asked to type into the chat
